analyticalMisses.note: Pitched effectively from a run-prevention standpoint but failed the 6+ K threshold; five-inning/88-pitch outing and recent IL return were relevant workload/efficiency risks.
Threw 8 dominant scoreless innings but finished with only 4 strikeouts. The K loss cannot be blamed on workload -- good run prevention must not be treated as equivalent to strikeout production.
Substantive handicap miss rather than a close variance loss. Washington won 7-0; Cade Cavalli dominated and Kevin Gausman struggled.

Meaningful process downgrade warranted. Field-of-Dreams pitcher-usage uncertainty was raised pregame and the recommendation was already reduced but remained the favorite wager. Bradley lasted only 4 innings (3 Ks, 5 R, 7 H, 4 BB) -- performance independently justified the early hook (not the venue itself), but workload-dependent K probability was still too confidently estimated under elevated uncertainty.

analyticalWins.note: Cleaner expression of the Boston/Tolle game handicap than Tolle 6+ Ks; Boston led after five even though the K prop lost.
Cleaner expression of the PHI-MIN handicap than Bradley's K prop; Philadelphia won 7-1.
Well structured -- could win without requiring poor pitching performance. Nola pitched effectively and struck out nine yet still recorded only 15 outs.

gameLevelConcentration.note: Boston F5 (won) was a cleaner expression of the Boston/Tolle game handicap than Tolle 6+ Ks (lost) -- Boston led after five even though the K prop lost.
Substantive handicap miss: Washington won 7-0; Cade Cavalli dominated and Kevin Gausman struggled.

Philadelphia ML (won) and Aaron Nola NO 18+ outs (won) were cleaner expressions of the PHI-MIN handicap than Taj Bradley 6+ Ks (lost), which carried elevated Field-of-Dreams-venue pitcher-usage uncertainty flagged pregame.

processErrors.lesson: The day's loss was concentrated entirely in pitcher strikeout overs.
processErrors.note: All three K props lost and consumed \$60, while all non-K markets combined were profitable (3-1, +\$20.36, ~+30.39% ROI).

processErrors.lesson: Do not conclude from one slate that strikeout props should be abandoned; treat the result as evidence that the K-prop manual process needs stronger decomposition.

proposedInvestigations.lesson: Future K analysis should explicitly separate: projected batters faced/workload; recent pitch count and injury/return context; opponent lineup-specific K propensity and handedness; pitcher K%, whiff/swinging-strike skill and pitch mix; command/walk/pitch-efficiency downside; early-hook and unusual-venue risk.
Do not claim a specific venue (e.g. Field of Dreams) caused an early hook without independent performance evidence -- verify against actual runs/hits/walks allowed first.
